content: The document titled Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management is a publication by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2020. It includes additional indicators and is available in an electronic version with the ISBN 978-92-4-000438-2. The publication is licensed under Creative Commons, allowing users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the work for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. The suggested citation for this publication is provided, and it forms part of the WHO guidelines on HIV strategic information. The publication is made publicly available for transparency and informational purposes, in line with the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition, 2014). The document includes specific programmatic indicators, such as: 1. Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)-related ARV toxicity: This measures the percentage of PrEP users who discontinued or interrupted PrEP due to serious antiretroviral (ARV)-associated toxicity during the reporting period. The numerator (N) is the number of individuals who discontinued or interrupted PrEP due to toxicity, and the denominator (D) is the total number of individuals on PrEP during the reporting period. 2. Opioid Substitution Therapy (OST) retention: This indicator tracks the percentage of individuals receiving OST who continued treatment for at least six months. The numerator (N) is the number of individuals from the cohort still in treatment six months (and 12 months) after starting OST, and the denominator (D) is the number of individuals who started OST during the cohort recruitment period. 3. Service coverage for prisoners: This measures the number of individuals in prisons or other closed settings who receive HIV prevention or treatment services. Specific sub-indicators include: Number of clean needles and syringes distributed to prisoners. Number of prisoners receiving OST. Number of condoms distributed to prisoners. Number of prisoners receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART). Number of prisoners tested for HIV. Number or percentage of prisoners living with HIV. Number or percentage of prisoners with hepatitis C or co-infected with HIV and hepatitis C. 4. ARV medicine stock-outs: This indicator measures the percentage of ART sites that experienced stock-outs of any antiretroviral drugs during the reporting period. The numerator (N) is the number of ART sites with stock-outs, and the denominator (D) is the total number of reporting ART sites. 5. Early Infant Diagnosis (EID) turnaround time: This measures the percentage of EID test results returned within four weeks of specimen collection. The numerator (N) is the number of EID tests conducted with results returned within four weeks (or less, based on national standards), and the denominator (D) is the total number of EID tests conducted during the reporting period. A two-day limit is considered an acceptable alternative. 6. HPV vaccination coverage among women living with HIV: This indicator tracks the number of women living with HIV who have received the complete HPV vaccine series. The numerator (N) is the number of women living with HIV who completed the vaccine series, and the denominator (D) is the estimated number of female survey respondents living with HIV. 7. Discriminatory attitudes towards people living with HIV (PLHIV): This measures the percentage of individuals aged 15–49 who exhibit discriminatory attitudes towards PLHIV. The numerator (N) is the number of survey respondents who answer no to either of the following questions: Would you buy fresh vegetables from a shopkeeper or vendor if you knew that this person had HIV?
